lines.u1: You type a U R L. The browser splits it into scheme, host and path, and checks its caches.
lines.d1: No luck, so it asks D N S. The resolver walks from the root, to the dot com servers, to the authoritative server.
lines.d2: The answer is an I P address, and every step along the way caches it.
lines.t1: Next, a T C P connection: the browser sends a SYN, the server answers SYN ACK, and the browser confirms with an ACK.
lines.t2: Then T L S agrees on encryption keys, so everything after that is private.
lines.s1: The request lands on a C D N edge server near you, which answers with the static H T M L straight from its cache.
lines.s2: That page points to C S S and Java Script bundles with hashed names, which can be cached for a year.
lines.r1: The browser builds the D O M, and downloads the C S S and Java Script in parallel.
lines.r2: The first paint shows the app shell, while the data is still on its way.
lines.g1: Now the Java Script calls the A P I: a fetch to the Go backend, over the same secure connection.
lines.g2: Go routes the request to a handler, through middleware, queries the database, and answers with J S O N.
lines.h1: The Java Script turns the J S O N into elements, and the browser lays out and paints the finished page.
lines.outro: D N S, T C P, T L S, a static shell from the edge, one call to a Go A P I, and a render. Usually in well under a second.
